concepts.definition: Runs one block of code if a condition is true, and the other block if it is not.
concepts.example: if (digitalRead(2) == LOW) { LED on } else { LED off } picks one of two paths depending on the button state.
concepts.pitfall: Putting ';' at the end of the if (...) line: the if does nothing and ends, and the code inside the curly brackets always runs.

concepts.definition: == compares two values and gives true or false; = assigns the value on the right to the variable.
concepts.example: durum == LOW asks "is durum LOW?", while durum = LOW makes durum LOW.
concepts.pitfall: Writing if (durum = LOW): durum is always 0, so the condition is never true.

concepts.definition: && is true if both conditions are true, || is true if at least one is true; ! takes the opposite of the condition.
concepts.example: buton && egim is true only while both inputs are pressed.
concepts.pitfall: Mixing up "and" and "or" logic; the difference between them only shows when exactly one input is active.

concepts.definition: A variable type that holds only true or false.
concepts.example: bool basili = (digitalRead(2) == LOW); stores whether the button is pressed.
concepts.pitfall: Forgetting that pressed = LOW with INPUT_PULLUP and setting up the bool value the wrong way round.

concepts.definition: A choice between many paths that jumps to the case line matching a variable's value.
concepts.example: switch (kod) { case 1: ... break; case 2: ... break; default: ... } picks a path depending on the value of kod.
concepts.pitfall: Forgetting break: the program runs the code of the next case as well.

quiz.prompt: a and b are two bool variables. In how many of the four possible combinations of a and b is the expression (a || b) && !(a && b) true?
quiz.explanation: Try the four combinations one by one: for (false,false) the first part is false; for (false,true) and (true,false), a||b is true and a&&b is false, so the expression is true; for (true,true), a&&b is true, so the expression is false. There are 2 true combinations: the expression means "exactly one is true".

The program enters the case 2 line and D12 lights. There is no break at the end of case 2, so the program falls through into the code of case 3 and lights D11 too; the break there stops it. To light only D12, a break would have to be added to case 2.

if (durum = LOW) is not a comparison but an assignment: it puts 0 into durum and the condition counts as 0, that is false. The else always runs and the LED never lights. It should be if (durum == LOW). The other lines are correct.

quiz.prompt: The button is between D2 and GND, and the pin is INPUT_PULLUP. Which of these means "the button is NOT pressed"?
quiz.explanation: When not pressed, the pin is HIGH, so it is not equal to LOW: digitalRead(2) != LOW is true. The first option says the button is pressed. The second option says it is not HIGH, which means it is pressed. The third option is an assignment.

x = 7 meets both the x > 3 and the x > 5 conditions, but the chain stops at the first true condition. Because x > 3 comes first, sonuc = 1 and the else if is never evaluated. If you want the result 2, the order of the conditions must be changed.
